findings.claim: Q3 is declared an inference item (ELF-TYPE-002) but its key restates a proposition the passage asserts outright, and the stem's premise — the panel disagreement — does no work in selecting it; the WHY-KEY argues a further proposition ("mouths differ") that option C does not contain.
findings.evidence: Stem: "What is implied by the disagreement inside Quennerly’s panel?" Key C: "Some of the ashy finish is made in the taster’s own mouth, not the glass." The passage states this directly, one sentence before the disagreement is introduced: "The sugar comes off in the mouth. Enzymes in saliva, and the bacteria alongside them, cut the phenol loose, and it reaches the nose from behind, after the glass has been put down." The disagreement ("Six of the twenty-four mark the ashy finish harder than the rest, year after year; one tasted the worst lot of the vintage and called it clean") is only reached in the NEXT sentence. The rationale's own inferential step is "the release happens in the mouth, and mouths differ; so part of what is scored is contributed by the taster" — the second and third clauses are the inference, and neither appears in C. The generator's self_blind_solve records that Q3's key was moved precisely to avoid retrieval: "Q3's key originally restated the six sensitive tasters literally, which would have been retrieval rather than inference".
findings.why: Family labelling and the retrieval/inference split are pedagogy-stage business, and a SOUND verdict certifies that the item tests what it says it tests. Here a student who never reads past "cut the phenol loose" answers Q3 correctly, so the unit's only ELF-TYPE-002 slot is filled by a second detail item and the block's declared question geometry ("Q3 inference") overstates its range. It stays minor because C is still the single best option, no distractor becomes defensible, and no student is mis-keyed — the defect is in what the item measures, not in whether it is right.

findings.claim: The verdict was upgraded from CORRECTED (round 1) to CLEAR (round 2) on a Q2 that did not change, and Q2 still breaches binding addendum rule 5's "options ≤8 words" — a breach the shipped rationale states in plain text.
findings.evidence: BRIEF-ADDENDUM.md rule 5: "in any multi-question unit at least one short-breath question (short stem, options ≤8 words). ELF longs too, where natural." Q2 option word counts: A=8, B=8, C=8, D(key)=9 ("They take up the phenols and keep them there."). Q2 rationale: "this is the unit's short-breath item (short stem, options of eight or nine words)". No other question in the unit has options under 12 words (Q1 15–17, Q3 13–16, Q4 12–15, Q5 15–16), so the unit has no rule-5-conforming short-breath question. Diffing candidates-final-round1/elf-b16-001.json against candidates-final/elf-b16-001.json shows exactly ONE change between the two rounds — the Q4 WHY-KEY sentence — and nothing in Q2.
findings.why: Rule 5 is a form rule the language stage is positioned to enforce, the fix is one word ("and keep them there" → "and keep them"), and the same stage returned CORRECTED against the same text a round earlier. Nothing in the file records a decision to invoke rule 5's "where natural" hedge for ELF longs, so CLEAR reads as the breach having been missed rather than adjudicated. Minor because the breach is one word on one option, carries no student-facing harm, and the hedge would in fact excuse it if invoked explicitly.

findings.claim: The metadata's M-TELL self-certification is false under word count at Q2, where the key is the unique longest option — and it was accepted a second time when the verdict moved from MINOR_FIXES to SOUND.
findings.evidence: generator_meta.key_letters: "The key is never the strict-longest option in any of the five questions (M-TELL 0/5)." Q2 words: A=8, B=8, C=8, D=9, key=D. Under character count Q2's longest is C (54 chars) against D (45), which is why the mechanical gate recorded "gate": "M-TELL", "verdict": "pass" in verdicts.jsonl. The other four questions do check out on both metrics (longest by chars: Q1 D, Q3 B, Q4 D, Q5 D; keys B, C, A, B).
findings.why: "Pick the longest option" is the canonical test-wise heuristic pedagogy review exists to defeat, and Q2 is the one item whose options are otherwise length-matched, which is what makes a single extra word visible. The practical tell is weak — by bulk on the page a solver's eye lands on C ("a smoke-affected harvest") — so the item is not solvable without reading; the defect is that a false self-certification in the shipped metadata was taken at face value twice rather than checked against the metric a solver actually uses.

findings.claim: The one sentence Q4's key hangs on uses "a reading" in a sense its immediate context makes ambiguous — a dissenting taster's score versus a laboratory reading — and both Q3's and Q4's rationales silently take the laboratory sense.
findings.evidence: Passage ¶3: "Quennerly is untroubled by the spread. “The median is the only figure that has ever predicted what a drinker will say,” she says, “and a reading that contradicts it should give way.”" The antecedent in the two preceding sentences is intra-panel spread ("Six of the twenty-four mark the ashy finish harder than the rest"; "one tasted the worst lot of the vintage and called it clean"), so "a reading" reads first as an outlying taster's score. Q4's rationale takes the other sense: "After Quennerly's claim that a contradicting reading \"should give way\" he writes \"She is right about that\"", keyed to A, "He backs the panel outright where its verdict and a reading disagree." The passage does use "read"/"reading" for instrument output elsewhere ("One washed lot even read a little higher"; "The January readings were unremarkable"; "on a reading and a nervous buyer").
findings.why: Cross-checking a key's load-bearing sentence against the rationale that cites it is the integrated sweep's core move. The key survives the ambiguity — the writer's very next sentence supplies the laboratory sense himself ("The January readings were unremarkable and the January wines were not"), and A is independently secured by "Thickness of smoke is no guide either" and by his calling the shed ferments "the sensible answer" — so no student can be mis-keyed. It is recorded because a complaining student could point at the sentence and argue the writer only endorsed a statistical claim about her own panel.

findings.claim: Two round-1 integrated findings survive verbatim into the round-2 shipping file, including a provenance statement in originality_note that the batch's own artifacts disprove; the round-2 integrated record carries no note payload, so there is no evidence either was adjudicated rather than missed.
findings.evidence: (a) originality_note: "a sibling batch16 unit (gen-elf-short-2) independently took 'Brindlow' for its byline". gen-elf-short-2 is elf-b16-004 ("Sixpence a Night"), whose byline is Aveline Hemblow and whose own note says the reverse: "'Brindlow' (rejected late under law 13, because at the time of this pass the sibling batch16 unit gen-elf-long held the surname for its chemist, Corin Brindlow; gen-elf-long has since renamed that character Corin Pemberdine". (b) Passage ¶5 still reads "Growers ferment five kilograms from each block in a shed the week before picking ... because ten days of that is the shortest honest test anybody has" — seven days of lead time cannot contain a ten-day minimum. Both texts are byte-identical to candidates-final-round1; the only round-2 edit anywhere in the file is Q4's WHY-KEY. reviews/integrated.jsonl records only {"verdict": "MINOR_NOTES"} with no findings field.
findings.why: MINOR_NOTES is the right severity band for both items, so the verdict itself is not refuted — but the record cannot be checked against them, and the false provenance line is the exact text a V-FINAL name re-verification is supposed to re-run from (the unit's own note flags all three surnames "FLAGGED FOR V-FINAL RE-VERIFICATION"). The substantive outcome is safe: no batch16 unit ships "Brindlow", and Pemberdine, Quennerly and Kettlestrand appear in no sibling passage.
